title: 1 Samuel 23:15–18
context: In the wilderness of Ziph, Jonathan comes to David and strengthens his hand in God. He affirms that David will be king, and the two renew their covenant before the LORD. It is the last recorded meeting between them.

verses.text: David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life. David was in the wilderness of Ziph in the woods.
verses.arminianNotes: David sees that Saul has come to seek his life, and he hides in the woods of Ziph. Arminian readers note that even a man of faith feels the pressure of real danger, which sets up Jonathan’s visit.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers observe that David’s fear is honest, and God meets it through a friend. The verse prepares for one of the tenderest scenes in the book.

verses.text: Jonathan, Saul’s son, arose and went to David into the woods, and strengthened his hand in God.
verses.arminianNotes: Jonathan goes to David and strengthens his hand in God. Arminian readers see a model of friendship that points a discouraged believer back to God, a ministry every Christian can offer another.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that Jonathan strengthens David not in himself but in God. True encouragement directs people to God’s promises, which Jonathan does at real cost to his own claim to the throne.

verses.text: He said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for the hand of Saul my father won’t find you; and you will be king over Israel, and I will be next to you; and Saul my father knows that also.”
verses.arminianNotes: Jonathan says David will be king and he will be next to him. Arminian readers admire Jonathan’s humility in yielding his own prospects, though his hope of standing beside David was not realized, since he died with Saul (31:2).
verses.reformedNotes: Jonathan says even Saul knows David will be king. Reformed readers see in this the certainty of God’s purpose, recognized even by those who resist it, and Jonathan’s willing submission to God’s choice.

verses.text: They both made a covenant before the LORD. Then David stayed in the woods and Jonathan went to his house.
verses.arminianNotes: The two make a covenant before the LORD, renewing earlier pledges (18:3; 20:16-17, 42). Arminian readers see covenant friendship freely chosen and faithfully kept, even when loyalty to David put Jonathan at odds with his father.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the covenant is made before the LORD, with God as witness and guarantor. David later honors it by showing kindness to Jonathan’s son (2 Samuel 9).
